when: Range sums, running aggregates, in-place index tricks, Kadane-style scans.
tpl:
pre = [0] * (n + 1)
for i, x in enumerate(a):
    pre[i+1] = pre[i] + x
# sum of a[l:r] is pre[r] - pre[l]
trap: Off-by-one on the 1-based prefix offset. Write the invariant `pre[i] = sum of the first i elements` above the loop and check it against l = 0.

when: You need O(1) lookup of “have I seen this?”, counts, or complements.
trap: Mutating the dict while iterating; forgetting that counts of characters need a fixed-size array when the alphabet is small.

when: Sorted input, palindromes, pair/triplet sums, in-place partitioning, merging.
cx: O(n) after an O(n log n) sort
trap: Duplicate triplets — skip equal neighbours after you record a hit.

when: Longest / shortest contiguous subarray or substring satisfying a constraint.
cx: O(n) — each index enters and leaves once
trap: A shrink condition that is not monotonic. Windows only work when growing can never fix a violation.

when: Sorted array, rotated array, or a monotone predicate over a numeric answer space.
cx: O(log n) × cost of the check
tpl:
lo, hi = min_ans, max_ans
while lo < hi:
    mid = (lo + hi) // 2
    if feasible(mid): hi = mid
    else:             lo = mid + 1
return lo
trap: Off-by-one from mixing inclusive/exclusive bounds. Pick one invariant (`lo` is the answer-or-left-of-it) and never deviate.

when: Next greater/smaller element, spans, histogram areas, expression parsing.
trap: Choosing strict vs non-strict comparison wrong — it changes which duplicates get matched.

when: “K largest/smallest”, merging k sorted streams, scheduling by priority, running median.
trap: Python's heapq is a min-heap — push negatives for a max-heap, and push tuples with a tiebreaker to avoid comparing unorderable payloads.

when: In-place reversal, cycle detection, merge, reorder, O(1) space constraints.
tpl:
prev = None
while head:
    nxt = head.next
    head.next = prev
    prev, head = head, nxt
return prev
trap: Losing the tail. Always use a dummy head when the first node can change.

when: Traversals, depth/diameter, path sums, LCA, validation, serialization.
trap: Validating a BST with only parent comparisons — you need an inherited (lo, hi) range.

when: Prefix search, autocomplete, word dictionaries, XOR-maximisation on bits.
tpl:
node = root
for ch in word:
    node = node.children.setdefault(ch, {})
node['$'] = True
trap: Memory blowup — use arrays of 26 only when the alphabet really is fixed.

when: Connectivity, islands, shortest path on unweighted graphs, flood fill, bipartite check.
trap: Marking visited on dequeue instead of enqueue — nodes get pushed many times.

when: Dependencies, course schedules, build order, cycle detection in a DAG.
trap: If `len(order) < V` there is a cycle — say so, don't return a partial order.

when: Dynamic connectivity, Kruskal's MST, grouping equivalent items, redundant edges.
trap: Union by size/rank matters — without it the tree degenerates to a list.

when: Dijkstra for non-negative weights, Bellman-Ford for negatives, 0-1 BFS for 0/1 weights.
trap: Dijkstra is wrong with negative edges. Say it out loud in the interview before you write it.

when: Enumerate all subsets / permutations / placements under constraints.
trap: Forgetting to undo state (`cur.pop()`), or appending `cur` instead of a copy.

when: Best value over a prefix, decisions per index, LIS, house-robber, coin change, stock problems.
tpl:
dp = [0]*(n+1)
for i in range(1, n+1):
    dp[i] = max(dp[i-1], dp[i-2] + a[i-1])
return dp[n]
trap: State that is not a function of the index alone — if you need “last taken index”, the state must include it.

when: Edit distance, LCS, knapsack, interval DP, unique paths, regex matching.
trap: Row-rolling to O(m) space before the 2D version works. Get it right, then optimise.

when: Scheduling, merging, jump games, minimum removals — when a local choice is provably safe.
tpl:
a.sort(key=lambda x: x[1])   # by end time
end = -inf; cnt = 0
for s, e in a:
    if s >= end: cnt += 1; end = e
trap: Not justifying the exchange argument. If you cannot argue why greedy is safe, reach for DP.

when: XOR tricks, subsets as bitmasks, single-number problems, power-of-two checks.
cx: O(n) or O(2^n · n) for bitmask DP
tpl:
x & (x - 1)      # clear lowest set bit
x & -x           # isolate lowest set bit
for s in range(1<<n): ...  # enumerate subsets
trap: Python ints are arbitrary precision — mask with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` when the problem implies 32-bit wraparound.

when: Rotations, spirals, in-place marking, game-of-life style updates.
trap: In-place updates that read stale/fresh values inconsistently — encode both states in one cell.

when: LRU/LFU cache, rate limiter, iterators, O(1) insert-delete-random, tweet feeds.
tpl:
# hash map -> doubly linked node, O(1) move-to-front
class Node: __slots__ = ('k','v','prev','next')
trap: Forgetting to unlink the node from the list when you evict — the map and the list drift apart.
